clue.text: Richer when not working

definitions.meaning: having more money, in a more comfortable position
read cryptically as a gambler (one who bets) who is off duty

explanation.definitionFit: Being more prosperous is being in a better financial position; the second reading treats a punter as a 'better' and 'off' as away from work.

clue.text: Fragrant resinous substance from the east found by the French on a motorway

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI with the figure read as a letter I

explanation.surface: A perfume ingredient imported from Asia turns up on a motorway with some French people.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first major motorway, from London to Leeds; crosswords read its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a tropical tree resin used in perfumes and varnishes, a fragrant gum.

clue.text: I sent a rum medicinal decoction

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so these letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone has sent along a peculiar herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old British adjective for odd, signalling an anagram of I SENT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal infusion, a brewed drink taken for health.

clue.text: Respect from clergyman in the past

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a clergyman
ere is an old word for before, previously

explanation.surface: Admiration for a vicar of former days.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep esteem and honour.

clue.text: Calf cavorting round ring of the central point

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing the ring
cavorting means prancing about, so the letters of calf leap into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A young cow frisks in a circle around the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges CALF to FCAL, and 'round' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Focal describes what relates to a focus, the point everything centres on.

clue.text: Casual one from France camping on Scottish island left

parts.note: un is French for one
camping means staying in a tent: in tent
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A relaxed Frenchman has gone off camping on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Casual is used in its sense of accidental, not done on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual remark can be one made by chance, with no deliberate aim behind it.

clue.text: Creating a favourable impression whilst crowding round the sheriffs men

indicators.note: round says the crowding word goes around the sheriff's band

parts.note: crowding means pushing or pressing in on
a posse is the band of men summoned by a sheriff in Westerns

explanation.surface: A Wild West scene of a crowd pressing round the sheriff's deputies, making a good impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attractive or appealing on first meeting is said to be engaging and winning in appearance.

clue.text: Unremitting anxiety about hospital treatment

parts.note: intensive means thorough and concentrated, never letting up
care in the sense of worry or concern

explanation.surface: A patient frets nonstop about being treated in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hospital unit and regime where critically ill patients receive constant monitoring.

clue.text: Treatment needed when there's trouble afoot

definitions.text: Treatment needed when there's trouble afoot

parts.words: Treatment needed when there's trouble afoot
parts.note: 'trouble afoot' normally means something bad is brewing, but read literally it is trouble in the feet, which calls for a foot specialist's care

explanation.surface: Some remedy is called for when mischief is brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of medicine treats ailments of the feet, such as corns and bunions.

clue.text: Going round in a canter in the flesh

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters circling and coming back in a different order

explanation.surface: A rider trots a horse around a ring for real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' signals an anagram of IN A CANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarnate means embodied, given bodily form, existing physically.

clue.text: Back one coming from the subcontinent

parts.note: hind means rear, at the back
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A rear guard's single member arrives from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi, a language of northern India, is also used as an adjective for things of that region.

clue.text: Outspoken Lynn holds up a flower

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the sound of the name takes the next word inside it
outspoken here means spoken aloud, so the name is used for how it sounds

parts.note: the name Lynn sounds like the letters L-I-N

explanation.surface: A forthright woman called Lynn raises a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' says the name is used only for its sound, and 'holds' puts the next word inside that sound; Lynn is a woman's name, not the Norfolk town.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Nut be allowed to return

indicators.note: to return means the word for allowed comes back, read the other way

parts.note: let means allowed, permitted

explanation.surface: A nut is permitted to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses only the word for allowed; 'be' stays as written in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel nut is the seed of the areca palm, chewed as a mild stimulant in Asia.

clue.text: Spring tied

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a big leap and secured or fastened with cords.

clue.text: Test case

definitions.meaning: a court case, a hearing before a judge

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a try-out to check something works and a legal hearing in court.

clue.text: The French name Kay heartlessly as being awkwardly tall

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the name is taken out

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman names a gangly girl called Kay unkindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips the central A from KAY, leaving KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky describes a person who is thin and gangly, long-limbed without grace.

clue.text: Make a sound come-back for at least the second time

definitions.text: Make a sound come-back for at least the second time

parts.words: Make a sound come-back for at least the second time
parts.note: a sound returning from a wall is a repeated noise; doing it again means a further round of reverberation

explanation.surface: Ask a performer to make a comeback once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverberate again: a returned noise that is itself returned once more.

clue.text: Enquire in Alabama about another state

indicators.note: in says the enquiring word is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Ala is the traditional abbreviation for the US state of Alabama
to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: Someone in Alabama asks after a different US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state, in the far north-west of the continent.

clue.text: Workers' tie

definitions.meaning: of a trade association of employees

explanation.definitionFit: A trade association protects employees, and the same word means a joining or link between things.

clue.text: Way of one from Afghanistan

parts.note: a path is a way, a track
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The route taken by a man from Kabul.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathans are the Pashto-speaking people of Afghanistan and north-west Pakistan.

clue.text: Easterner, after the start of the match, hurried round the point

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the kick-off letters

parts.note: KO is short for kick-off, the start of a football match

indicators.note: round says the word for hurried goes around the compass point

parts.note: ran means hurried
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: An Asian spectator rushes round the ground once the game kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a kick-off, abbreviated KO, is the start of the match; 'round' then wraps the word for hurried around the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Korea, in East Asia, is a native of the Far East.

clue.text: Put off the Spanish within 24 hours

indicators.note: within says the Spanish word sits inside the period of time

parts.note: a day is 24 hours
el is the Spanish masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Postpone the Spaniards for a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to defer or hold over until later.

clue.text: Show clearly that the Eastern Church does admit to having French wine

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so these words take the wine inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Proof that an Orthodox church confesses to stocking claret.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England, a common crossword abbreviation; 'admit to having' lets the wine in between the Eastern letter and the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to display or reveal a feeling or quality plainly.

clue.text: A commonplace statement somehow pointless in the hall

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are got into place by some unspecified means, rearranged
pointless means losing a compass point, here the south

parts.note: a truism is a statement so obvious it hardly needs saying

explanation.surface: A banal remark made in an entrance hall goes over badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops S (south) from A TRUISM, leaving ATRUIM; 'somehow' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central court or entrance space in a building.

clue.text: Doctor Love has no money to gloat over

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
no means nothing, the round figure O
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A doctor in love finds himself penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring 'love' means zero, hence O; L for pounds comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: To slobber over something is to show greedy, eager delight in it.

clue.text: Sole fruit?

parts.note: the flatfish called a sole has a citrus-named variety, so the fish's name reads as a fruit

explanation.surface: Asks whether there is only one kind of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow citrus fruit that also names a type of flatfish sold by fishmongers.

clue.text: Composer still endlessly confused about the last letter

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the final letter of the alphabet
confused means the letters are muddled into a new order
endlessly means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: still taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician still flustered about how to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STILL to STIL, 'confused' rearranges it as LIST, and 'about' wraps that around Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic pianist and writer of music.

clue.text: Sort of non-monetary remuneration

parts.note: 'sort of' hints at a kind, which is the final word of the phrase: reward made in goods or services instead of cash

explanation.surface: A form of wages without cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rewarded with goods or services rather than money is compensation in that form.

clue.text: Tunnel beneath the pit

parts.note: under means beneath
a mine is a pit, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: Dig a tunnel below the coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap a fortification by digging underneath it, burrowing to weaken it.
